subject: Automagically Create Space at Top of Histogram for Inset Plot

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Automagically Create Space at Top of Histogram for Inset Plot
parts:
Dears, 

I'm trying to add a subset histogram(s) at the top of my main histogram. I am able to do this with the following code. If I were to have a non-normal distribution, this inset plot would cover part of the main histogram. However, if I could programmatically add 20% to the y-axis I would be fine. The only way I can think of doing this is to dissect the ggplot_build() for the y_range, then adjust the y-scale. 

Is there a better way? 

p<-ggplot(data=mtcars, aes(x=mpg))+geom_histogram()

#dissect the guts for the range (default bins)
p.build<-ggplot_build(p)
p.build$panel$ranges[[1]]$y.range[2]

q<-p+scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,p.build$panel$ranges[[1]]$y.range[2]*1.2))


grid.newpage()
vp_main<-viewport(width = 1, height = 1, x = 0.5, y = 0.5)
vp_inset<- viewport(width =0.2, height = 0.2, x = 0.13, y = 0.88)
print(q, vp=vp_main)
print(p, vp=vp_inset)

Thanks,

Brandon

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: Re: Automagically Create Space at Top of Histogram for Inset Plot
parts:
a lazy workaround would be to add a geom_blank layer with the same stat as the histogram layer, but data scaled up.

HTH,

b.
